newsitem.title: UK: Metals slide from highs, most end LME lower.
newsitem.headline: Metals slide from highs, most end LME lower.

text.p: Base metal prices largely tracked lower during Friday afternoon LME trading, as copper turned tail above the $1,970 level, although aluminium managed to close in the plus column, traders said.

Aluminium was active, as the market continued its corrective rally away from a projected test of the $1,300 level, helped initially by a 6,375-tonne stock fall and latterly by news some Russian aluminium smelters were considering cutting production.
But traders were cautious over the Russian cuts, while after the market closed news emerged that Canada said there were no plans for a new MOU output cutting pact.
There had been some conjecture that the mooted production cuts in Russia were moves towards a new international effort to curb output, traders noted.
Three months prices finished at $1,337 a tonne, a $5 gain from Thursday's kerb close.
"It may bounce higher yet, but I remain dubious as the market does not have a lot going for it," a trader said.
Activity elsewhere, even in copper, was not particularly great as early upside moves faltered and end-week liquidation ate into the lead, zinc and nickel markets.
Copper peaked at $1,978 today, when the market was attempting to erode the overhead resistance above $1,970 yet again.

But with the 18,450-tonne stock fall widely expected and the cash/threes backwardation not tightening up from Thursday levels the market was hit by profit-taking. Prices finished the kerb at $1,957, down $1.
"Copper was looking a bit toppy in the $1,975/80 area and the volume was light," the trader said.
However, in the short-term, technical tightness may yet see $1,970 bested and the market running up to $2,000.
Zinc lost its footing between $1,030 and $1,040 and fell back to end at $1,026, down $7. Lead sagged as well, and was $16 easier at $751.
Tin drifted lower, but trading was undramatic with the market closing at $6,060, down $15.
Nickel fell back after touching resistance around $7,200, and was $70 lower at $7,150.
Alloy was indicated at $1,207/12 a tonne, against Thursday's close of $1,200.
